title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and moved swiftly through their agenda after first opening the floor to public comment and then later addressing parking issues on North Avenue.

After Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order the group heard from Lisa Erbacher.  She wanted to earn the council’s permission for the All-American Boy and Girl contest at Charley Brown Park on July 4th and for the Ice Cream Social on Friday, August 7 at the Gazebo in Library Park.  Concerning the All-American Boy and Girl contest, Erbacher referred to longevity of the event and paid homage to Jan Phillips and others dating back decades.  She mentioned they could use some volunteer judges and will seek contestants in the days ahead.  Commissioner Phil Wiley made a motion to approve her request and the council quickly approved the measure.  Erbacher then turned to the Ice Cream Social on Friday, August 7 at the Gazebo in Flora’s Library Park.  The event also includes Flora First Methodist Church grilling hot dogs and live music from a local band.  She talked about the increasing popularity of the event and is encouraged by a family event that brings local residents together for fun and fellowship.  Commissioner Lacey Lewis made a motion and members approved Erbacher’s request.  Before moving on, City Administrator Mike Stanford took a moment to thank Lisa Erbacher for all that she does including cleaning up the downtown area in recent days and wanted everyone to know about her efforts.

Next, resident Anthony Krutsinger addressed the council about the recent $10,000 purchase of Flock Cameras that read license plates.  Krutsinger said he believes they are an invasion of privacy and an overreach by government to track and monitor citizens who have not committed any offense and are simply going about their lives.  He questioned how police are using the existing Flock devices and was told by Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger that they have already helped in the safe recovery of two people who went missing with Dementia as well as identifying stolen plates and aiding in the investigation of recent thefts and for other purposes.  Krutsinger refocused his thoughts on the $10,000 cost and stated that the expense is not needed when the city has not even built a sidewalk to Walmart.  City Administrator Mike Stanford countered his argument about the money by saying the sidewalk projects are part of an $800,000 grant from the State of Illinois that take a long period of time before there’s any construction.  Concerning the cost, Stanford restated Chief Ruger’s remark about safely recovering two Dementia patients and changed it up by saying what it they were children?  What would be the cost of a human life?  Krutsinger closed by asking the council to rethink adding additional cameras and seek additional input from residents.  He said many people are against expanding their use.  He was grateful for the opportunity to share his opinion.

As the meeting continued, Mayor Spicer asked commissioners to approve the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included past meetings and the warrant list for the last half of May.  The measures were approved unanimously.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer, straining to make herself heard due to her hoarseness wanted to thank Flora Tourism and others for putting on the Community Market or Farmer’s Market which just got started.  She appreciates their effort and encourages residents to embrace it Saturday mornings at Library Park.  As the mayor polled commissioners for their comments, Phil Wiley echoed the mayor’s comments about the Community Market and is heartened by the activity in the downtown area this spring and hopeful that it continues as we move into summer.  Wiley also took a moment to encourage volunteers to lend a hand to Flora Tourism for the July 4th activities at Charley Brown Park.  He says they need help both Saturday and Sunday, even if it’s for short periods to help with the entry gates, the inflatables and many other areas.  Commissioners Jim Fehrenbacher used his time to congratulate Flora Athletes.  He noted the Doubles pairing of Kyler Dennis and Luke Powless advanced to round 4 of the ISHA State Tennis Finals before succumbing to the team from Chicago St. Ignatius.  And Wolves standout athlete Kehlin Crawford earned glory for himself and Flora High School as the Champion of the IHSA Class 1A State High Jump competition, with a jump of 6’7.5”.  Congratulations on your success.

Flora Police Jeremy Ruger asked the council to approve an ordinance to amend no parking zones on several streets in Flora to improve traffic flow and for the safety of pedestrians.  With little discussion, commissioners approved his request.  Specifically, the Flora City Council banned parking on…

East North Avenue (both sides) from Stanford Rd. to Sycamore St.

West North Avenue (both sides) from Elm St. to Greenlaw Blvd.

Campbell St. (West side) from West North Avenue to West Third St (adjacent to pickle ball courts)

Locust St. (East side) from East Third St. south to alleyway.

In the absence of Lee Beckman with Milano and Grunloh Engineers of Effingham, Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford updated the council on the latest concerning Flora’s grant applications.  The work on the Safe Routes to School Sidewalk project in Flora is underway on Shadwell St.  He said the city has learned that Flora has secured the next round of grant money for sidewalks, but it will be quite a while before any construction moves forward.  The city is seeking grant money to reline several sewer lines in the city.  There is survey work to be done on Worthey for sidewalk construction work to Walmart.  And Flora’s OSLAD Grant for Rotary Park has been approved, but there’s no timeline for a start date.  In other action, the council approved the sale of real estate at   315 Austin Ave., 847 W. Maple and 144 Shady.

City Clerk Kaci O’Dell encourages everyone to participate in the ICash Discover What’s Yours event coming to the Flora Volunteer Fire Department on West Second St on Tuesday, June 9 from 10:00am-2:00pm.  It’s your chance to learn if you have unclaimed cash or property.  Illinois State Senator Jason Plummer is teaming up with Illinois Treasurer Michael Frerichs to help citizens find lost money or other property.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles took a moment to remind everyone that the Flora Swimming Pool opened to the public last Monday with 200 swimmers taking advantage of the opportunity.  He adds the water is warming up and invites swimmers to visit them in Charley Brown Park.

As the meeting drew to a close, Superintendent of Public Services Toby Rinehart had a handful of personnel actions requiring council approval.  All were approved without dissent…

Dustin Edgington from Gas Utility to Meter Reader at $36.49 per hour.

Jarrad Hildebrand from Meter Reader to Gas Utility 1st Year Apprenticeship at $35.89 per hour.

Trenton Brown from Wastewater Operator to Street Operator at $31.09 per hour.

Commissioners also approved a job posting for a Wastewater Operator (Swing Shift) at $35.38 per hour.

title: GRAIN BIN DEATH
full_story:
Wabash County Sheriff J. Derek Morgan reports that Monday morning at approximately 9:24 am Wabash County 911 received a call in reference to 3 men being trapped in a grain bin at Friendsville Avenue and North 1550 Boulevard in Mt. Carmel.

The Wabash County Sheriff’s Office, Mt. Carmel Police Department responded along with Mt. Carmel Fire Department, Wabash General EMS, and Firefighters with Patoka Township Fire and Rescue responded.

When crews arrived, 2 of the three were able to get out of the grain bin.  Rescue crews worked diligently trying to get the remaining man.  At approximately 1 pm the man was extricated from the grain bin.  Wabash County Coroner Shaun Keepes pronounced 21-year-old Steven D. Haase, of Mt. Carmel, deceased at the scene.

title: EFFINGHAM MAN TO THROW OUT FIRST PITCH
full_story:
Today is Lou Gehrig’s Day in Major League Baseball, and an Effingham man and his family will be helping observe the special day.

Today marks the date of Gehrig’s death in 1941 at age 37.  Gehrig died from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or ALS.  The disease became known as “Lou Gehrig’s Disease”.  Gehrig, one of the best ever to play the game and a physical specimen in his playing days, died less than two years after his diagnosis.

At Wrigley Field in Chicago, a host of activities are planned as the Cubs take on the Athletics.  One of the participants will be Phil Flach of Effingham, who has been diagnosed with ALS.  Phil is being hosted by Cubs TV broadcaster John “Boog” Sciambi, who had a friend die from the disease, and Phil will be throwing out a first pitch at tonight’s game.

Major League Baseball is working to draw attention to ALS.  Each game played today will observe the date.

While Phil is battling ALS, his wife Karen is working to create awareness of the disease. She is reaching out to those in the community who have been touched by ALS, and will be working to heighten awareness of resources, as well as efforts such as Leon’s Legacy, that raises funds for caregivers of those dealing with ALS.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
USDA’s crop progress and condition report released June 1st showed 91% of corn and 89% of soybeans were planted in Illinois with 80% and 75% emerged, respectively.

There were 5.6 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending May 31st. Statewide, the average temperature was 71.6 degrees, 4.5 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged .25 inches, 0.77 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 6% very short, 27% short, 59% adequate, and 8% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 25% short, 61% adequate, and 9% surplus.

Corn planted reached 91%, compared to the 5-year average of 92%.  Corn emerged reached 80%, compared to the 5-year average of 81%.  Corn condition was rated 1% very poor, 4% poor, 30% fair, 56% good, and 9% excellent.

Soybeans planted reached 89%, compared to the 5-year average of 85%.  Soybeans emerged reached 75%, compared to the 5-year average of 68%.  Soybeans condition was rated 1% very poor, 4% poor, 31% fair, 55% good, and 9% excellent.

Winter wheat headed reached 92%, compared to the 5-year average of 94%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 2% very poor, 6% poor, 22% fair, 59% good, and 11% excellent.

title: FCC SOFTBALL STANDOUTS
full_story:
Frontier Community College Athletic Director Jeremy Ellis announced that three members of the FCC Bobcats Softball team have earned postseason honors from Region 24 and the Great Rivers Athletic Conference.

Lexi Miller was named Second Team All-Region 24 as a pitcher, while Peyton Smith was named Second Team All-Region 24 as an outfielder.  In the Great Rivers Athletic Conference, Smith and Harper Holeman earned First Team honors, while Miller was named Second Team.

Miller will continue her academic and athletic career at Kentucky Wesleyan College in Owensboro, Kentucky.

Smith, a freshman outfielder from Johnston City, Illinois, led the Bobcats with a .341 batting average and started all 55 games.  Holeman, a freshman infielder from Princeton, Kentucky, started 56 games, finishing with a .276 batting average in 174 at-bats.

title: HOUSER AT DU QUOIN
full_story:
Country music powerhouse Randy Houser is headed to the Du Quoin State Fair Grandstand on Monday, September 7th, bringing his unmistakable voice and chart-topping catalog of hits to Southern Illinois for an unforgettable night of country music.

Known for smash hits including “How Country Feels,” “Runnin’ Outta Moonlight,” “Boots On,” “Goodnight Kiss,” and “We Went,” Houser has earned a reputation as one of country music’s most commanding vocalists.  The New York Times praised his voice as “wholly different, thicker and more throbbing, a caldron bubbling over.”

“Randy Houser has one of those voices that instantly grabs your attention, and his live shows bring incredible energy to the stage,” said Illinois Department of Agriculture Director Jerry Costello II.  “We’re excited to welcome him to Du Quoin and know fairgoers are going to love this concert.”

Houser has amassed more than one billion streams throughout his career and earned critical acclaim for his powerful delivery of the Top 5 hit and CMA Song of the Year-nominated “Like A Cowboy.”  Beyond music, Houser has showcased his talent on the big screen, appearing in Killers of the Flower Moon directed by Martin Scorsese and starring Leonardo DiCaprio, and also in Dennis Quaid’s The Hill.

“Randy Houser’s catalog is packed with songs fans know and sing along to, and he brings an authentic country sound that fits perfectly at the Du Quoin State Fair,” said Du Quoin State Fair Manager Luke Davison.  “This is going to be a great night of live music at the Grandstand.”

Tickets for the Randy Houser concert will be available Friday, beginning at 10 am via Ticketmaster.  Tier 3 tickets are $35, Tier 2 tickets are $40, Tier 1 tickets are $45.

The Du Quoin State Fair runs from August 28th through September 7th.  To learn more, visit dsf.illinois.gov/.

title: CELLPHONE BAN
full_story:
Governor JB Pritzker says he will sign a bill to ban the use of cellphones in IL schools.

Senate Bill 2427 requires all public and charter school districts to adopt and implement policies restricting student cellphone use during instructional time.

The bill was passed by lawmakers and aims to reduce distractions in the classroom and improve student focus and mental health.

title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corporation’s Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) still has funding available.  Applications for the current program year will be accepted through August 14th.

Households that applied on or after October 1st, may only reapply if facing utility disconnection.  Those who previously received reconnection assistance should contact their local CEFS Outreach Office to check eligibility for additional help.

Since October 1st, CEFS has approved $537,216.00 in energy benefits for 716 Clay County households, averaging $750 per household.  An additional 229 households received $168,613 in emergency reconnection assistance, averaging $736.

Monthly Income Eligibility are as follows: 1 person can make up to $3,332 per month, 2 people can make up to $4,357 a month, 3 people can make up to $5,382, and 4 people can make up to $6,407 per month.  Income limits for larger households are available at www.cefseoc.org or www.liheapillinois.com.

To schedule an appointment, contact the CEFS Clay County Outreach Office at 618-662-4024 which is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am – 4:30 pm, or schedule online at www.cefseoc.org.  Applications can be completed in person or by phone, and documents may be submitted in person, by mail, or electronically.  Those needing any special accommodation should contact their local CEFS office.

LIHEAP is funded by the US Department of Health and Human Services and the Illinois Department of Commerce & Economic Opportunity.  CEFS administers the program in Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie, and Shelby counties.

title: APRIL UNEMPLOYMENT
full_story:
The Clay County unemployment rate for April was 4%, down from 5.2% in March and .2% higher than the same month, one year ago.  The numbers translate into 5,736 in the labor force, 159 less than March.  There were 229 unemployed, 80 less than last month.

All area counties had lower unemployment rates in April from March.  Effingham County had the lowest rate in the are at 3.3% down from 4.5% in March.  Followed by Jasper County at 3.4% down from 4.2% last month.  The lowest unemployment rate in the state is in Monroe County at 2.6% and the highest in the state is again in Edwards County where the April rate was 11%, down 3.9% from the previous month.

The Illinois Department of Employment Security reported that total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 175 jobs in April 2026.  Employment gains were posted by employers in the Construction, Manufacturing, Government, Trade-Transportation-Utilities, and Professional-Business Services sectors.  Payroll losses were seen in the Private Education-Health Services, Financial Activities, Information, and Other Services sectors.

The state unemployment rate for April was 4.7% down from 5.2% the previous month and up from 4.2% a year ago.  The US unemployment rate for April was 4%, down from 4.3% the previous month and up from 3.9% in April of last year.
